Collage Studio: codec corresponding-source and recombination materials
=====================================================================

This directory replaces, rather than attempts to identify, the unknown binary
revisions in heic2any 0.0.4 and the npm AAC encoder's embedded FFmpeg. No opaque
upstream codec artifact is used by the application's imports. Historical package
licenses are retained in public/third-party-notices.txt for attribution.

Actual source inputs
--------------------
libheif 1.19.8 + libde265 1.0.16: HEVC/HEIC decode, LGPL-3.0-or-later.
FFmpeg 7.1.1: built-in AAC-LC encode, libavcodec + libavutil, LGPL-2.1-or-later
with permissive portions. GPL/nonfree/external libraries/autodetection disabled.
AAC wrapper and C bridge: published @mediabunny/aac-encoder 1.61.3 source, MPL-2.0.
Shared AAC/bitstream source: Mediabunny commit
9d36fc5779b254904bc609e66f2cd80ed8390b4b, MPL-2.0.
Mediabunny core 1.61.3: complete published source archive retained for MPL source
availability. It is a separate application dependency pinned by the root lock.
Emscripten + emsdk 4.0.9: pinned build tools and runtime source. The emsdk release
mapping pins upstream toolchain release cb2a69bce627bd2247624c71fc12907cb8785d2f.

Every downloaded input is present in sources/, listed with an observed SHA-256
and its exact download URL in sources.lock.json. These are new rebuild inputs;
they are NOT assertions about the revision of the old opaque WASM. The npm AAC
archive is retained as original source provenance; its precompiled dist/ is
never extracted into or referenced by the actual build.

Original license texts remain in licenses/ and the original archives. Full
per-file notices and copyrights remain in the corresponding source archives.
The two relocated AAC encoder imports and the local worker adapter are MPL-2.0
modifications. Shared helper code, worker, C bridge and original copyrights
are retained. Local HEIC adapters use the application license; neither changes
the LGPL licenses of the codec libraries.

Build from complete application source
--------------------------------------
Prerequisites on Linux/macOS: Bun (version from the release's packageManager),
Bash, Python 3, curl, tar (with gzip/xz support), cmake, make, pkg-config,
autoconf, automake, libtool, and patch. Emscripten is installed by the script;
no existing host FFmpeg/libheif installation or Docker runtime is required.
First toolchain installation needs access to Emscripten's download service.
Use ordinary HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY environment variables if needed. Never
publish proxy credentials or signing credentials. Source archives ship offline;
the compiler toolchain itself is installed from the pinned emsdk manifest.

From the root of the exact release source tree:
  bun install --frozen-lockfile
  bun scripts/license-codecs.mjs download
  bun scripts/license-codecs.mjs build
  bun run build

The root application build must invoke the codec build before Vue type checking
and Vite. Do not run two codec builds concurrently. CODEC_BUILD_JOBS defaults
to 2 and may be increased explicitly. CODEC_FORCE_REBUILD=1 forces recompilation.
No network request is made by the installed codecs at runtime: both generated
modules contain their own WASM, and the AAC Worker is bundled locally by Vite.
HEIC converts the first top-level image to a real PNG, with RGBA/orientation
handled by libheif. AAC retains the upstream CustomAudioEncoder behavior and
is registered by the existing application fallback when native AAC is absent.
AAC uses WASM SIMD. Actual device behavior must be tested; build scripts are
not themselves behavior verification or a claim of byte-identical output on
arbitrary host systems.

Generated artifacts and release gate
------------------------------------
The generated HEIC module, AAC module/worker, static codec libraries and bridge
objects are recorded by SHA-256 in build-receipt.json. The receipt also binds
all shipped codec sources, patches, source locks and build scripts. Unrecorded
scratch edits cannot enter a build: each build freshly extracts the pinned
C/C++ archives into .work/. A changed source or generated binary invalidates
the receipt. There is no fallback to a prebuilt npm blob when a rebuild fails.
The build also refreshes a bounded generated section in
public/third-party-notices.txt from the exact shipped Emscripten/musl/LLVM runtime
license originals. Other attributions and sections remain untouched. Include
that refreshed notice in web/native assets, not a notice from an older build.

After building the frontend/native application:
  bun scripts/license-codecs.mjs release release

This command refuses absent/stale artifacts and creates:
  release/collage-studio-codec-corresponding-source.tar.gz
  release/collage-studio-codec-corresponding-source.tar.gz.sha256

The archive includes exact complete codec sources, locally modified MPL files,
all build/download/recombination scripts, original license texts, generated
artifacts, build receipt, the actual libheif/libde265/libavcodec/libavutil static
libraries, and non-library bridge objects. It excludes scratch paths/toolchain
installations. Do not replace this kit with links to upstream HEAD. Publish the
kit and its checksum next to EVERY corresponding Android/iOS/Linux binary,
including AUR/Snap/GitHub downloadable releases, and the web build. Publish the
exact FULL application source (including src/, assets, package.json, bun.lock,
Vite/PWA config, native project, and native Cargo lock) alongside it too: the
codec kit alone is not the application-source/recombination delivery.
AUR/Snap packaging must use that source release and preserve third-party notices;
GitHub release assets must include both native artifacts and this kit. Tauri
must bundle dist-native/ locally, including the notice and generated worker/assets.
Keep the source kit available for as long as required by the applicable licenses.
A sourcekit URL, source offer, or notice alone is not evidence of publication.

Modification and recombination
------------------------------
Recipients may edit the shipped local wrapper/HEIC bridge/application source.
For library edits, put ordinary unified diffs relative to the library root in:
  third_party/codecs/patches/libheif-1.19.8/*.patch
  third_party/codecs/patches/libde265-1.0.16/*.patch
  third_party/codecs/patches/ffmpeg-7.1.1/*.patch
Patches are applied with -p1, included in the source kit and receipt, and retained
when the build refreshes scratch sources. Do not edit .work/ as a source of truth.
Then run CODEC_FORCE_REBUILD=1 bun scripts/license-codecs.mjs build and rebuild
the app. This recreates the combined work from modified library source.
For direct relinking, source .work/emsdk/emsdk_env.sh after installing the pinned
SDK and use the exact em++/emcc linker invocations in license-build-codecs.sh,
replacing the corresponding relink/*.a with your own modified static library.
The shipped relink/heif-bridge.o and relink/aac-bridge.o are the non-library
bridge objects; their C sources are also supplied. Rebundle the AAC worker with
Bun and rebuild Vite using the complete application source. A directly modified
binary cannot use an old build receipt; rebuild through recorded sources/patches
before redistributing a new release and generate a new corresponding-source kit.

Installation information and recipient rights
---------------------------------------------
No project EULA may forbid replacement of LGPL-covered components or reverse
engineering for debugging their modifications. Linux builds need no publisher
secret: build with the shipped Tauri/Cargo/frontend source and install your own
package or run the locally built binary. Android recipients can build/sign
with their OWN Android SDK and keystore; to install over the publisher-signed
app Android requires the same key, so export .collage drafts first and uninstall
the old app or choose a different identifier for side-by-side installation.
No publisher signing secret is necessary or distributed. iOS builds need Xcode,
the recipient's OWN provisioning/development signing and an allowed device;
Apple's platform restrictions remain real, and we do not claim sideloading or
App Store acceptance has been verified. Complete unsigned native source/build
settings must remain available. A distributor who introduces an installation
lock must separately supply any installation information needed under LGPLv3;
this kit does not waive that requirement or promise legal compliance.

Not a legal opinion: exact source identity and concrete rebuild/recombination
paths are engineering evidence. Successful native/web builds and real HEIC/AAC
smokes are release prerequisites; this file does not claim they have occurred.
